purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Find the panel that does the thing I want
finding: The rail shows six destinations - Insert, Layers, Pages, Media, Content, Brand - but the editor has twelve panel destinations. Templates, Components, AI, Publish, History and Review render in the same drawer and are on no rail button; the only ways in are a bare letter key (T, Shift+A, I, U, H, R), the Cmd+K palette, or a row in the top-bar overflow menu. A user who has used Templates once has no persistent handle to get back to it, and nothing on screen says the six on the rail are half the list.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/rail/tabsConfig.ts:349-351 RAIL_FIGMA = one group of 6 ids [add, layers, pages, assets, content, design]; GROUPED_TABS_CONFIG:72-262 declares 13 tabs; packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/TabRouter.tsx:125-244 renders 12 of them in the drawer (settings is fullpage-only). Off-rail doors: LeftSidebar.tsx:202 getFigmaRailGroups, useSidebarKeyboard.ts:34-48 bare letters, shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx:49-62 'Open X panel', shell/SiteMenu.tsx:190-252. Searched: 'RAIL_FIGMA', 'getFigmaRailGroups', 'railMode', 'zone'.
fix: Decide the spine first: either promote the six off-rail panels into the rail (grouped, with a divider) or give the rail an explicit 'More' entry that lists every panel with its shortcut. Do not leave six destinations reachable only by memorised keys.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Know which panel is open / which one I last used
finding: When the drawer is closed no rail button is marked selected - aria-selected is bound to 'active AND drawer open', and the accent bar only renders in that same condition - so the rail reports a tablist with nothing chosen. Worse, arrowing through the rail with the drawer closed changes the active tab and opens nothing: the keyboard handler calls the tab-change callback but never the drawer toggle, so a keyboard user silently reassigns what the next rail click will open with zero visible change.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:137-138 (isVisibleActive = isSelectedTab && drawerOpen), :153 aria-selected={isVisibleActive}, :160 bar rendered only when isVisibleActive; :458-481 handleKeyDown calls safeTabChange(tabId) with no onDrawerToggle; :437-449 handleBtnClick is the only path that opens the drawer. The dim 'ls-btn--last' class exists (LeftSidebar.css:189) but carries no accessible state.
fix: Keep the selected rail item marked whether the drawer is open or shut (open/closed is a separate signal from selected), and make rail arrow-keys either move focus only (manual activation) or open the panel they select.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Leave the editor
finding: The most prominent control on the left is a chevron and the word 'Exit' - it never says where it goes. It navigates to DASHBOARD_URL + '/dashboard/projects', and in the standalone build DASHBOARD_URL falls back to the current origin, so on localhost:5050 the loudest button in the shell walks the user to a route that does not exist on that origin and the editor is gone with no in-app way back. The overflow menu's old 'Exit to dashboard' row - the one that named the destination - was deliberately removed as 'dead weight'.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/Topbar.tsx:177 exitLabel default '\u2039 Exit', :201-203 the button; packages/editor/src/editor/shell/StudioHeader.tsx:489-491 exitToDashboard -> window.location.assign(`${DASHBOARD_URL}/dashboard/projects`); packages/editor/src/shared/utils/runtimeEnv.ts:68-77 DASHBOARD_URL falls back to window.location.origin; packages/editor/src/editor/shell/SiteMenu.tsx:15-16 records the removal of the named row. Searched: 'onExit', 'exitToDashboard', 'Exit to dashboard', 'DASHBOARD_URL'.
fix: Name the destination on the control ('Exit to dashboard' / the workspace name) and show it in the exit-confirm dialog. A control that removes the whole application should say what it removes it to.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Run a command I cannot find in the UI
finding: There are two command palettes with two chords and two different command sets. Cmd+K opens the shell palette (panel navigation, undo/redo, zoom, registry commands); Cmd+Shift+P opens a second, canvas-owned palette (edit, view, insert, tools). A user who learns one never sees the other's rows, and the cheat sheet lists both as if that were a feature.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx:1-8 (Ctrl+K) and packages/editor/src/editor/canvas/hooks/useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:35-62 (Cmd+Shift+P, its own window listener); packages/editor/src/editor/shell/hooks/useEditorShortcuts.ts:28-31 states the split as intentional; canvas/controls/KeyboardCheatSheet.tsx:89-90 prints both. Searched: 'CommandPalette', 'metaKey && e.shiftKey', 'cmdOpen', 'isPaletteOpen'.
fix: One palette. Merge the canvas commands into the Cmd+K list (they are already registry-backed) and retire Cmd+Shift+P, or keep both surfaces but make them show the same rows.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Learn the keyboard
finding: Two separate keyboard-help screens exist and neither is complete. '?' opens a canvas cheat sheet (selection, navigation, positioning); Cmd+/ opens an app shortcuts panel (panels, edit, view). The split is documented in three places as deliberate, which means a user pressing '?' to ask 'what are the shortcuts' gets half an answer and has to know a second chord to see the rest. Neither screen mentions the plain single-letter rail keys (A I T M L P B S U H R D) that actually switch panels - the shortcuts panel prints them only as bare letters in a 'Panels' group with no explanation that they need no modifier.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/canvas/controls/KeyboardCheatSheet.tsx:27-101 (6 groups) and packages/editor/src/editor/panels/KeyboardShortcutsPanel.tsx:26-68 (3 groups, PANEL_SHORTCUTS derived from GROUPED_TABS_CONFIG); shell/hooks/useEditorShortcuts.ts:33-41 and shell/SiteMenu.tsx:136-141 both narrate the split. Searched: 'KeyboardCheatSheet', 'KeyboardShortcutsPanel', 'showShortcuts', "e.key === '?'".
fix: One shortcuts screen, grouped by surface, opened by both '?' and Cmd+/. Show the bare-letter panel keys with an explicit 'no modifier' note.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Zoom / redo from the command palette
finding: The Cmd+K palette prints chords that do not exist. 'Fit to view - Ctrl+0' is wrong: Cmd+0 sets 100% and Cmd+1 is the fit. 'Redo - Ctrl+Y' is not what the product advertises anywhere else (Cmd+Shift+Z). The same wrong-chord defect was found and fixed in the canvas palette and in the shortcuts panel, with comments explaining it; this third copy was left. The palette also lists Undo twice, as 'Undo' under Edit and 'Undo last action' under History, both running the same call.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx:132-136 (view-fit, 'Ctrl+0'), :83 ('Ctrl+Y'), :68-88 vs :139-148 (two Undo rows); the real bindings are canvas/CanvasFooterToolbar.tsx:241-255 (Cmd+1 fit, Cmd+2 selection, Cmd+0 100%). The corrections already made elsewhere: canvas/hooks/useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:154-158 and panels/KeyboardShortcutsPanel.tsx:57-66.
fix: Derive every printed chord from one shortcut registry rather than three hand-typed lists, and drop the duplicate Undo row.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Fix the 17 warnings the top bar is counting
finding: The issues counter is a permanent top-bar chip and the first thing a user is told to act on before publishing, but the panel it opens goes nowhere. Every issue row is wired to a handler that only closes the panel - it does not select the element, switch page, or open Brand. With 17 warnings in the demo, clicking any of them dismisses the panel and leaves the user exactly where they started, with no indication that nothing happened.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/AquibraStudio.tsx:625 onSelectElement={() => setIssuesOpen(false)} with the comment 'v1 just closes'; the panel renders each row as an interactive Row whose onClick is that handler (shell/IssuesPanel.tsx:238-243). The chip copy that promises action: chrome-ui/IssueChip.tsx:52-59 'review before publish'. Searched: 'onSelectElement', 'IssuesPanel', 'setIssuesOpen'.
fix: Either give each issue a real destination (element + page) or stop making the row look clickable - an inert row that closes the panel is worse than a row that says 'no location'.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Read the issues while looking at the page
finding: The Issues panel is an absolutely positioned 360px slab pinned to top:56 / right:0 with z-index 45. It covers the whole 300px inspector plus 60px of canvas, so you cannot see the element an issue is about while the list is open. The 56px top offset assumes nothing sits above the top bar, but the recovery banner, the load-error banner and the 48px review bar all render in the same column - with any of them present the panel starts 40-90px too high and overlays the bar it should sit under. It is also the only right-hand surface that is not part of the grid, so nothing pushes over for it and no click-outside dismisses it.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/AquibraStudio.tsx:604-616 (position absolute, top 56, right 0, width 360, zIndex 45); the bars above it at :478 RecoveryBanner, :479 LoadErrorBanner, :533 ReviewBar (h-12, shell/ReviewBar.tsx:36); the inspector column is rail/LayoutShell.css:82-88 var(--layout-inspector-width, 300px) at z-index var(--bk-z-drawer)=20 (themes/tokens.generated.css:141).
fix: Make Issues a real column in the shell grid (or a drawer that shares the inspector slot with a back affordance), so the canvas is still visible and the offset is not hand-computed.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Check what my visitors will see before publishing
finding: 'Quick preview' does not preview the site - it previews one page, with everything turned off. The overlay renders composer.exportHTML().combined, which is the ACTIVE page only, inside an iframe with sandbox="" - the fully-restricted value, so no scripts run and nothing can navigate. A user clicking a nav link in preview gets nothing; a user checking a click animation gets nothing (the engine deliberately injects an interaction runtime into that document, and the sandbox forbids it from running); a user checking their other four pages has to close the preview, switch page tabs, and press preview again. The only control is a 'Done' pill.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/AquibraStudio.tsx:199-212 (handle -> exportHTML().combined); packages/editor/src/engine/Composer.ts:685-717 combined = one page's html + css, with the interaction-runtime script injected at :700; packages/editor/src/editor/shell/PreviewOverlay.tsx:104-109 <iframe sandbox="" srcDoc={html}>. Searched: 'UI_TOGGLE_PREVIEW', 'previewHtml', 'sandbox', 'exportHTML'.
fix: Preview the SITE: render every page, keep the page switcher in the overlay, and allow scripts and same-frame navigation so links and interactions behave. If a locked-down preview is required, say so on screen ('links and scripts are disabled in preview').

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Ask the AI for help
finding: AI has two homes and which one you get depends on the door. Cmd+J, the inspector's AI chip and the canvas selection toolbar emit ui:switch-tab {tab:'ai'}, which the shell intercepts and renders AI as a drill-in over the RIGHT inspector. Bare 'I' and the Cmd+K row 'Open AI panel' set the left panel tab to 'ai', which renders AITab in the LEFT drawer. Same feature, two positions, two ways back, in the same session.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/StudioPanels.tsx:291-300 (ui:switch-tab 'ai' -> setAiInInspector(true), returns before the left-panel path) and :493-502 (AITab in LayoutShell.Inspector); the left-drawer path is sidebar/TabRouter.tsx:141 case 'ai' reached from sidebar/useSidebarKeyboard.ts:34-48 with tabsConfig.ts:93 shortcut 'I' and shell/modals/CommandPalette.tsx:49-62 -> EVENTS.UI_PANEL_OPEN -> shell/hooks/useEditorEventListeners.ts:145-155 (VALID_LEFT_TABS includes 'ai').
fix: Pick one home for AI and route every door to it. If the inspector drill-in is the answer, make bare 'I' and the palette row open that, and remove the 'ai' case from the left TabRouter.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Open the assistant from the top bar
finding: The rail configuration declares that the AI assistant lives in the top bar ('placement: topbar', label 'Ask AI') and the rail comment says AI is reachable from 'the canvas selection sparkle + Cmd+K'. The Topbar component has no AI control at all - its children are exit, site name, save, live chip, review pill, tools (preview/comments/issues), presence, notifications, publish, menu - and the overflow menu's 'Ask AI' row is rendered only in the legacy four-tool rail mode, which is off by default. In the shipped shell there is no persistent, visible AI entry point anywhere.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/rail/tabsConfig.ts:314 assistant placement 'topbar'; :337 the comment; packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/Topbar.tsx:12-13 enumerates the ten children and :176-337 renders exactly those - no AI branch; shell/StudioHeader.tsx:832 onAskAI={viewMode.fourToolRail ? onShowAI : undefined}. Searched (case-insensitive) in Topbar.tsx and StudioHeader.tsx: 'sparkle', 'ask ai', 'assistant', the sparkle emoji - only a prop comment at StudioHeader.tsx:88 matches.
fix: Give AI one persistent visible door and make the config describe it truthfully - either build the top-bar affordance the config claims, or move the declaration to wherever AI actually lives.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Change my site's settings
finding: Two things are called settings. The overflow menu's 'Site settings' row and the Ctrl+, chord open a 560px modal with three tabs (General, Canvas, SEO). A separate full-page Settings surface with thirteen screens - including its own Site settings and SEO screens - exists and is reachable only by pressing bare 'S', by the Cmd+K row 'Open Settings panel', or by the menu's 'Plugins' row, which deep-links into one of its sub-screens. A user who wants Domains, Redirects, Forms, Headers or Localization will look in the row named 'Site settings', not find them, and have no signal that a bigger surface exists.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/SiteMenu.tsx:193-197 'Site settings' -> onOpenSiteSettings; shell/AquibraStudio.tsx:508 onOpenProjectSettings={modals.openProjectSettings} -> shell/modals/ProjectSettingsModal.tsx:36-45 (three tabs); the full-page surface is sidebar/tabs/settings/screens/ (13 files incl. SiteSettingsScreen.tsx and SeoScreen.tsx), reached via tabsConfig.ts:187-201 (mode 'fullpage', shortcut 'S') and AquibraStudio.tsx:511 onOpenPlugins -> openLeftPanelToTab('settings','plugins'). Searched: 'ProjectSettingsModal', 'SettingsTab', 'openProjectSettings', 'openSiteSettings'.
fix: One Settings destination. Point 'Site settings' and Ctrl+, at the full-page surface and fold the modal's three tabs into it, or rename the modal to what it actually edits.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Get back to the canvas after visiting Settings
finding: Full-page mode replaces the canvas and the inspector, but it is entered from tabs that have no rail button, so the rail shows six items with none of them lit while the whole work surface has been swapped out. There is no global 'back to canvas' - the only way out is whatever close control the tab itself drew - and closing does not return the user to where they were: it hard-codes a jump to the Insert tab.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/StudioPanels.tsx:254-258 effectiveFullPageMode, :364-372 handleFullPageClose -> onLeftPanelTabChange('add'); rail/LayoutShell.css:193-201 fullpage collapses canvas+inspector; the rail's active test is id-equality against the 6 RAIL_FIGMA ids (sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:137) and 'settings' is not one of them (rail/tabsConfig.ts:350).
fix: Give full-page surfaces a persistent shell-level 'Back to canvas' and return the user to the panel they came from, not to Insert.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Open the editor on a laptop or a narrow window
finding: The layout stylesheet reserves a breakpoint for viewports under 1024px and its only content is a comment saying a warning overlay is 'handled by component'. No such component exists. Below 1024 the shell simply squeezes: rail 60 + drawer 280 + inspector 300 leaves under 400px of canvas, and the desktop frame has a 1024px floor, so the page is scrolled horizontally inside a lane a third its width with nothing telling the user the editor is desktop-only.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/rail/LayoutShell.css:353-358 (empty @media (max-width: 1024px) with the 'handled by component' comment); the desktop floor is canvas/canvasStyles.ts:57. Searched for the promised component: '1024', 'too small', 'minimum width', 'min-width supported', 'desktop only', 'larger screen' across editor/, shared/ and themes/ - the only hits are file-size math, device presets and this comment.
fix: Either build the small-viewport state (a blocking message naming the minimum width) or delete the promise. Today the product silently degrades into an unusable layout.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Make the panel wider to see what I am working on
finding: The drawer has exactly two widths and no way to choose anything in between. It is 280px, or - if the panel's header happens to carry an expand toggle - 700px, a jump of 2.5x. There is no drag handle on the drawer edge anywhere in the sidebar. At 1440 the expanded state leaves rail 60 + drawer 700 + inspector 300 = 1060, so the canvas lane is about 380px while the desktop page frame has a 1024px floor: expanding a panel to read it pushes the page the user is editing into heavy horizontal scroll, and the only way back is the same toggle. Two panels ignore the toggle entirely and set their own widths (Media 560, Templates 700) from runtime events.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:580-587 (panelWidthOverride: media override, then templates override, then isExpanded ? 700 : null) and :231 in sidebar/LeftSidebar.css (.ls-panel width: var(--drawer-w, var(--bk-size-drawer))); the toggle is chrome-ui/PanelHeader.tsx:46-51 (only rendered when a tab passes onExpandToggle). The desktop floor is canvas/canvasStyles.ts:57 (BREAKPOINTS.desktop.minWidth). Searched sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx and LeftSidebar.css for 'resize', 'Resize', 'onMouseDown', 'drag' - no resize affordance exists.
fix: Give the drawer a draggable edge with a remembered width, or at least a middle step. And when a panel takes more than half the canvas lane, say what it costs (or let the canvas re-fit) instead of silently pushing the page off-screen.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Understand what a 'tab' means in this editor
finding: The shell has two tab strips that mean completely different things and are marked up identically. The rail is role=tablist / role=tab and switches PANELS; the bar at the foot of the canvas is also role=tablist / role=tab and switches PAGES. To an assistive-technology user (and to the accessibility snapshot of a live run, which read the shell's tabs as 'Insert, Layers, Pages, Media, Content, Brand, Home') the two collapse into one list, so the homepage appears to be a seventh rail destination. There is no rail item named Home.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:606-610 (nav role='tablist' aria-label='Editor navigation') and :150-156 (Button role='tab'); packages/editor/src/editor/shell/PageTabBar.tsx:220-223 (role='tablist' aria-label='Site pages') and :229-235 (role='tab', aria-label `${page.name}, Homepage`). Searched for a rail Home button: '"Home"', '>Home<', 'aria-label="Home' across editor/ - the only rail hit is LeftSidebar.tsx:467, the Home KEY in the arrow-nav handler; the accessible name 'Home' comes from PageTabBar.tsx:234.
fix: Give the two strips distinct roles and names ('Editor sections' vs 'Site pages'), and make the page bar read as page navigation rather than as more of the same tabs.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Add, rename or delete a page
finding: Page management exists twice. The bar at the canvas foot switches pages, adds one with '+', and carries a right-click menu with Rename, Duplicate and Delete; the Pages rail panel is a separate surface for the same job with its own list, its own creation flow and its own command palette. A user has to learn which one holds which capability, and nothing on either says the other exists.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/PageTabBar.tsx:212-410 (tab list, add button, context menu with Rename/Duplicate/Delete, F2 rename, Shift+F10 menu) vs sidebar/tabs/pages/PagesTab.tsx reached from rail/tabsConfig.ts:139-150; a third page picker exists at sidebar/tabs/pages/components/PageCommandPalette.tsx:140. Searched: 'PageTabBar', 'PagesTab', 'createPage', 'setActivePage'.
fix: Decide which surface owns page management. Keep the foot bar as a pure switcher (switch + '+') and put every destructive or structural action in the Pages panel, or the reverse - but not both.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Move the keyboard focus off the canvas
finding: Once focus is inside the canvas, Tab is captured to cycle canvas ELEMENTS and preventDefault is called, so Tab can never leave the canvas. Escape only clears the selection. The documented way out is F6 region cycling, which appears in neither help screen - the cheat sheet lists Tab as 'Next element' and says nothing about escaping. The skip link at the top of the shell is called 'Skip to Canvas' and drops the user straight into the trap.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/canvas/Canvas.tsx:660 (wrapper tabIndex=0, onKeyDown=handleKeyDown) and canvas/hooks/useCanvasKeyboard.ts:87-107 (Tab -> e.preventDefault(), cycles elements); Escape at :249-253 only clears; the exit is shell/hooks/useEditorShortcuts.ts:91-95 F6 -> shell/regionCycle.ts:83-95; the skip link is rail/LayoutShell.tsx:302-304. Searched: "e.key === 'Tab'", 'cycleRegion', 'F6', 'skip-link'.
fix: Let Tab leave the canvas (use arrow keys, already bound, for element traversal) or print the escape chord on the canvas region and in both help screens.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Turn on element names / detailed inspection on the canvas
finding: The canvas reads an 'inspector mode' flag that switches hover from a bare outline to full element labels, and persists it to localStorage. The control that sets it is never rendered anywhere, so the mode is permanently stuck at its stored value (default off) and there is no door to turn it on. The unused component also binds bare 'I' - the same key the rail uses to open the AI panel.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/canvas/Canvas.tsx:291 const { isInspectorEnabled } = useInspectorMode() (consumed, passed to CanvasOverlayGroup); the setter lives on the InspectorToggle COMPONENT at canvas/controls/InspectorToggle.tsx:90-147, whose only references are its own file and the barrel canvas/controls/index.ts:16. Searched: 'InspectorToggle', 'useInspectorMode', 'setInspectorEnabled', 'buildrick-inspector-mode' - no JSX call site.
fix: Either give the mode a control (it belongs beside the other view toggles in the canvas bar) or delete the flag and the storage key. A persisted setting with no UI is a setting nobody can use.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Understand why I cannot publish
finding: The one blocked state in the shell announces itself only on hover. When publishing is refused the button keeps the full accent-blue primary treatment and is marked aria-disabled with the reason in a tooltip - there is no visual difference from a publishable site. A user looking at the bar cannot tell 'ready to ship' from 'publishing is not switched on for this workspace' without pointing at the button and waiting.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/Topbar.tsx:295-321 (the disabled branch renders <Button aria-disabled='true' className={PUBLISH_BTN_CLASS}>, and PUBLISH_BTN_CLASS at :38 is 'tw:h-8 tw:px-5 tw:text-[13px] tw:font-medium' - no colour or opacity change); the reasons come from shell/lifecycle.ts:104-109. Corroborates the prior finding SH-A-02 in docs/design-jobs/findings/SHELL-A.jsonl, re-verified at HEAD.
fix: Show the block without hovering - the reason belongs beside the button (or in the save/status cluster), not inside a tooltip.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Find the button that ships my site
finding: The single filled button changes its verb and can vanish. It reads 'Publish', 'Publish changes', 'Publish anyway', 'Send for review' or 'Open feedback' depending on derived lifecycle state, and when the site is live with nothing waiting the derivation returns null and the button is not rendered at all - replaced by a small green 'Live - domain' link earlier in the bar. A user who has learned 'the blue button on the right ships my site' finds an empty slot there and a link they did not associate with publishing.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/lifecycle.ts:141-250 (five labels; :246 returns null when published with no changes); shell/StudioHeader.tsx:801 publish={viewMode.readOnlyView || !nextMove ? 'hidden' : publish}; chrome-ui/Topbar.tsx:283 (hidden renders null) and :217-236 (the live chip that carries the state instead).
fix: Keep the control present and constant in position; let it say 'Published' / 'Up to date' in the settled state rather than disappearing. A CTA that leaves the bar teaches the user the bar moved.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Zoom in and out
finding: Zoom has three independent implementations that step differently. The footer's percentage flyout emits ZOOM_IN/ZOOM_OUT, which the canvas handles by adding or subtracting a fixed 10; the floating canvas bar binds Cmd+= / Cmd+- itself and jumps to the next entry in the preset list (10/25/50/75/100/150/200/400); the engine command registry has its own zoom commands again. From 100%, one path gives 110% and the other 150%, both from a control labelled 'Zoom in'. The clamp is also inconsistent: the presets and ZOOM_LIMITS stop at 400 while THRESHOLDS.ZOOM_MAX is 500.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/StudioFooter.tsx:273-280 (emitZoom ZOOM_IN/ZOOM_OUT) -> canvas/Canvas.tsx:403-419 (step by THRESHOLDS.ZOOM_STEP); canvas/CanvasFooterToolbar.tsx:256-265 (walks ZOOM_PRESETS); the third is engine/commands/defaultCommands.ts:461, whose own comment names the split; canvas/hooks/useCanvasCommandPalette.ts:74-84 records the diagnosis. Limits: shared/constants/canvas.ts:360-370 (max 400) vs shared/constants/config.ts:87-90 (ZOOM_MAX 500).
fix: One zoom owner with one stepping rule, and one clamp. Every zoom control should move the number the same way.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Come back tomorrow to the editor I left
finding: What the shell remembers is arbitrary. The active panel tab, its sub-tab and five canvas overlay toggles persist; the device and the zoom do not - they are plain state that resets to Desktop/100% on every reload, so a user working on the mobile breakpoint at 50% returns to a desktop frame at full size. The drawer's open/closed state is deliberately not persisted either. Three different storage mechanisms are in play: one JSON blob and two separate keys.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/hooks/useStudioState.ts:220-221 (device/zoom plain useState, not read from savedState), :225-246 (tab, sub-tabs and overlays read from savedState), :232-234 (drawer deliberately not persisted), :268-291 (savePanelState under 'buildrick-panel-state'); the other keys are shell/StudioPanels.tsx:232-241 'buildrick-inspector-shown' and canvas/controls/InspectorToggle.tsx:19 'buildrick-inspector-mode'.
fix: State one rule for what the editor remembers about a session (viewport included) and put it behind one store, so 'where I left off' means the same thing for every control.

task: Find a destination that is not on the rail
finding: The overflow menu carries about eighteen rows and is doing three unrelated jobs at once: it is the only persistent door to six in-editor panels (Review, Publish panel, Publish history, Templates, Components, Brand), it is the settings/export surface, and it is a launcher for six dashboard pages that open in a new browser tab. purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Take my site down
finding: 'Unpublish site...' does not open a confirmation. The row switches the left panel to the Publish tab and then, in the same tick, emits the unpublish request that the Publish tab is supposed to hear. That tab is lazily imported and mounts on a later render, so at the moment the event fires there is no listener - the user is moved to a panel they did not ask for and the confirm never appears. This is the exact race the codebase already documented and fixed once for the Pages 'From template' flow.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/StudioHeader.tsx:806-812 (onUnpublish -> onOpenPublish?.() then composer.emit(EVENTS.UI_UNPUBLISH_REQUEST) synchronously); the listener is sidebar/tabs/publish/PublishTab.tsx:182-192, and PublishTab is React.lazy at sidebar/TabRouter.tsx:42 (rendered at :190). The identical bug and its diagnosis: sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:393-401. Searched: 'UI_UNPUBLISH_REQUEST', 'ui:unpublish-request', 'onUnpublish', 'unpublishSite'.
fix: A destructive action must own its confirmation at the point of invocation - put the unpublish confirm in the menu's own flow rather than shipping the user to another panel and hoping it is listening.

task: Type on the page without triggering navigation
finding: Twelve panels are bound to bare, unmodified letters (A I T M L P B S U H R D), plus bare C for comment mode and bare ? for the cheat sheet. The rail handler skips inputs and contenteditable but does NOT stand down while a modal is open, unlike every other global handler in the shell - so a keypress inside a dialog that is not a text field can re-route the panel behind it. The letters come from rail/tabsConfig.ts:82,94,110,122,135,147,163,182,193,210,226,242,259.
fix: Add the modal guard, and show the letters where the user is (persistent rail labels or a one-line legend) rather than only on hover.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Turn a canvas overlay on or off
finding: Six overlay chords are bound globally, and one of them takes the browser's reload (Cmd+R -> Rulers). The comment says this was chosen deliberately because a printed chord must work, but the chords are printed only inside hover tooltips on a floating bar - so the cost (a user who reflexively presses Cmd+R gets rulers instead of a reload) is paid by everyone while the benefit reaches only the people who hovered. Cmd+B (Badges) and Cmd+' (Grid) sit on the same footing.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/canvas/CanvasFooterToolbar.tsx:215-280 (the global keydown; :271 rulers on plain Cmd/Ctrl+R, with the reasoning at :219-223); the chords are shown only via OverlayButton's Tooltip at :159-192.
fix: Do not take Cmd+R. Move the overlay chords onto a modifier the browser does not own, print them in the shortcuts screen, and keep the toggles' labels visible as they already are.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: Know what I have selected and get to it
finding: The footer is the shell's only always-on statement of what is selected, and it is read-only. It prints 'Section - Hero', a live pixel size and 'N elements selected', but none of it is a control: there is no way to jump to the element, clear the selection, or open it in Layers from there. The size is measured straight off the canvas DOM, so it silently prints nothing when the node is not rendered - a selected element on a hidden or offscreen region shows a name with no dimensions and no explanation.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/StudioFooter.tsx:210-224 (a <span> with a title, plus the dims span) and :79-87 elementDims returns null when the node is absent or zero-sized; the selection count comes from :144-164. Compare the top bar, where the review pill was deliberately made a door (chrome-ui/Topbar.tsx:364-383).
fix: Make the selection readout a door - clicking it should reveal the element (scroll to it and open Layers) - and say 'not visible' instead of dropping the size silently.

purpose: The editor shell - the frame every panel sits inside: top bar, left rail, canvas, page tabs and status footer. It is how a user knows where they are, moves between surfaces, controls the viewport, and gets into and out of the editor.
task: (module summary)
finding: PURPOSE: the shell is the frame - top bar, left rail, drawer, canvas, page tabs, status footer - that every other module is rendered inside. Its job is orientation (where am I, what is selected, what state is the site in), navigation (get to the right panel), viewport control (device, zoom, overlays), and entry/exit. PRIMARY TASKS: switch panels; switch pages; select and inspect on canvas; set device and zoom; read save/review/issue status; preview; publish or send for review; leave the editor. ENTRY POINTS: the dashboard's 'Edit site' link (unified editor at /edit/:id) and the standalone demo at localhost:5050/?siteId=; deep links via ?el= and ?page= (shell/hooks/useDeepLink.ts) and ?view=readonly / ?rail= (shared/utils/editorViewMode.ts:79-88). EXIT POINTS: the top-bar Exit (-> DASHBOARD_URL/dashboard/projects, behind a dirty/offline/stranded-mirror guard at StudioHeader.tsx:378-441), the overflow menu's six new-tab dashboard hand-offs, 'View live site', view-mode toggle (a URL navigation), and browser-chrome exits covered by a beforeunload guard. HANDS OFF TO: the sidebar panels (12 destinations via TabRouter, plus the full-page Settings/Media library via FullPageRouter), the inspector (and the AI drill-in that replaces it), the publish flow (PublishConfirmModal -> usePublishJob -> dashboard tRPC), the review flow (ReviewBar + Review panel + ReviewService), and the dashboard. RECEIVES FROM: the engine over the composer event bus (project load, selection, page changes, brand-dirty, publish/review status), the DS linter (the issue counts the chip shows), NotificationService and ReviewService. LANE VERDICT: the shell's biggest problem is not any single control - it is that the spine is only half-built. Six of twelve panel destinations have no persistent door; the two surfaces that should orient a user (the rail's selected state and the status footer) are inert; and three of the shell's own promises - preview shows the site, the issues chip leads to fixes, unpublish confirms - do not hold.
evidence: Read at HEAD across packages/editor/src/editor/{shell,rail,canvas,sidebar}, packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/Topbar.tsx, packages/editor/src/shared/constants/{canvas.ts,config.ts,layout.ts}, packages/editor/src/themes/tokens.generated.css and packages/editor/demo/main.tsx. git status checked first: the founder's uncommitted work is in the media/CMS area (dragPayload, useMediaState, MediaCommandLayer, Composer, ElementManager) and does not touch any file cited above; AquibraStudio.tsx was read only, never staged.
fix: Fix the spine before the surfaces: name the full panel list and give every destination a persistent door; make the rail and the footer say where the user is; and repair the three broken promises above.
